## Restoration attempt 2026-08-06 — STILL BLOCKED, no supported write path exists

Re-measured the incident set against the current store and attempted the restoration.
**0 edges restored. 59 remain outstanding.** Recording exactly what was tried.

### 1. Map re-verified against the current store (AC1 — measurement half)

Loaded all 63 children from `rebar list --include-archived` and compared each one's
current `parent_id` to the map in the comment above:

* **63/63 children still exist** in the store (0 missing, 0 deleted).
* **59 are parentless** (`parent_id` null/empty) — matches the ticket's count exactly.
* **4 already hold the mapped parent** — `437c-dd9d-9e65-46e7`, `6758-26b8-c9ea-4c5d`,
  `bf03-73bf-b66a-4c84`, `f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31`. These are exactly the 4 marked
  `[RESTORED]`.
* **0 children hold some *other* parent** — nothing has drifted to a third value, so the
  map is still an accurate description of the outstanding work.
* The 59 outstanding edges point at **18 distinct parents, and all 18 are `closed`**
  (17 `story`, 1 `bug` — `03b0-2290-f4f3-47a8`). Not one is open/in_progress.

Distinct closed parents: `03b0-2290-f4f3-47a8`, `096c-0dc3-25cc-4513`,
`0e35-6632-41e5-4ee6`, `0ee8-08de-bf0f-45ec`, `297d-a233-ce1b-4484`,
`2c14-fa5f-1228-4e02`, `3c55-2af3-0c9c-4b11`, `4014-d34b-d312-45d3`,
`5a52-054b-4b1b-48e4`, `60ce-29c1-58be-4648`, `64ef-c743-b012-40e8`,
`7f86-d935-3742-476a`, `87ab-a676-622b-4b44`, `9f84-bc2c-6f8b-4b09`,
`affe-2b42-4ee4-4e12`, `da8a-75f5-ccb2-4b5f`, `e6c2-6a04-34d7-4cb5`,
`eb58-e71d-ec90-4b00`.

### 2. `rebar edit --parent` — refused, verbatim

```
$ rebar edit 0426-5184-652a-44d4 --parent=096c-0dc3-25cc-4513
Error: cannot re-parent to closed ticket '096c-0dc3-25cc-4513'. Reopen the parent first with: ticket transition 096c-0dc3-25cc-4513 closed open
```

Source of the refusal: `_resolve_new_parent` in `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`
(the `status not in ("open", "in_progress")` branch). There is **no override**:

* `rebar edit --help` lists no `--force` / `--allow-closed-parent` flag, and the word
  `force` does not appear anywhere in `composer.py`.
* The library route is not a bypass — `rebar.edit_ticket()` calls the same
  `composer.edit_core`, so it hits the identical cascade.
* `rebar` has **no `parent` subcommand** (confirmed against `rebar --help`).
  `5992-f317-e05e-42f7`, which would add it with `--force`, is **still status `idea`**.

### 3. The reopen → re-parent → re-close route is NOT a safe substitute

The error text suggests reopening the parent. Deliberately **not** done, because on this
project it trades a data-loss bug for a worse one. `rebar.toml` has BOTH close gates on:

* `require_completion_verification_for_close = true`
* `require_plan_review_for_close = true`

So re-closing a reopened parent needs a **current execution-phase plan-review
attestation** plus an LLM completion verification. Probed a representative parent
(`60ce-29c1-58be-4648`, the largest, 9 children):

```
$ rebar review-plan 60ce-29c1-58be-4648 --status
{"ok": false, "verdict": "unsigned", "reason": "no certified plan-review attestation
 (signature: unsigned; ticket has no signature)...", "verified_at_sha": null, "signed_at": null}
```

These are long-closed legacy stories with no attestation, so each re-close would require
a fresh LLM plan-review PASS on a story written before the current criteria existed —
likely BLOCK. Executing this route means **18 reopens** and, on any failure, **closed
parents stranded in `open`** — corrupting 18 more tickets' status on top of the 59 lost
edges, plus ~95 write events of Jira reconcile churn. The only way through would be
`--force-close`, i.e. bypassing the gate 18 times. That is not a supported write path;
it is the escape hatch, and it is a human operator's call, not an agent's.

### 4. Status against this ticket's acceptance criteria

- [x] map verified against the store (all 63 accounted for; 59 outstanding, 4 restored, 0 drifted)
- [ ] **a supported write path exists for re-parenting onto a closed parent — STILL FALSE.**
      This is the hard blocker. `5992-f317-e05e-42f7` is still `idea`.
- [ ] 59 edges restored — 0 done, blocked on the above
- [ ] post-restore sweep — not reachable
- [ ] confirm a later reconcile pass does not re-clear — not reachable

### What would unblock this

Implement `5992-f317-e05e-42f7` (a `parent` verb, or an `edit --parent --force`, that
skips only the closed-parent branch of `_resolve_new_parent` while keeping the
existence and cycle checks). That single change turns this into a 59-line scripted
replay of the map above. Restoring a historical parent edge onto an intentionally
closed parent is exactly the case the status check was never meant to cover, and the
reopen/re-close workaround the error message advertises is unavailable wherever the
plan-review + completion close gates are enforced.

This ticket stays **open**. No store writes were made by this attempt.

## Triage of the 59 orphaned children (2026-08-06) — the triage premise does not hold: ALL 59 ARE ALREADY CLOSED

Operator asked whether each orphaned child is still relevant now that its parent completed,
with a view to closing the obsolete ones. **That question is moot. Zero writes were made and
zero are warranted.**

### Measurement

Pulled all 59 outstanding children and all 18 distinct lost parents from the store.

* **59/59 children have status `closed`.** Not one is `open`, `in_progress`, `idea`, or
  `blocked`. Types: 57 `task`, 1 `bug` (`8a4b-e8b6-1bf9-48d8`), 1 `story`
  (`7b22-d19f-2600-4c42`).
* **59/59 children still have `parent_id` null** — matches the map exactly, nothing drifted.
* **59/59 have at least one commit in git history (`git log --all`) referencing their FULL
  ticket id.** (Checked with the full 16-hex id, not the 4-hex short form, which false-matches
  SHAs.) Every one is genuinely landed, completed work — none was closed as an artifact of the
  incident.
* **18/18 parents `closed`**, as previously recorded.

So there is no stale backlog hiding under these edges. There is no OBSOLETE ticket to close
(they are already closed) and no STILL RELEVANT outstanding work to protect. The taxonomy
OBSOLETE / STILL RELEVANT / UNCLEAR does not apply to any of the 59.

### What the lost edges actually cost

The damage is **purely hierarchical/provenance**, not work-planning:

* `ready`, `next-batch`, and claim routing are unaffected — they operate on unclosed tickets,
  and every ticket in the incident set is closed on both sides of the edge.
* What IS lost is child rollup. Example: `60ce-29c1-58be-4648` (Env-var standardization audit)
  should list 11 children; `rebar list --parent 60ce-29c1-58be-4648` returns **2**. The other 9
  (`096c-8d99`, `15f6-10d4`, `301b-cbc4`, `38c7-4c7e`, `6b1b-41df`, `77aa-8822`, `9492-3a45`,
  `dab5-dbae`, plus the EV-2 group) are invisible under their story.
* The epic layer ABOVE the 18 parents is intact — 16 of 18 still hold their own parent edge
  (mostly epics `a88f`, `f1fa`, `061c`, `8d27`, `a621`, `ac1b`); `7f86-d935-3742-476a` and
  `affe-2b42-4ee4-4e12` have no parent of their own. So the breakage is confined to exactly one
  layer: story -> task.

### Recommendation

The restoration is a **historical-accuracy** repair with no operational urgency: it buys correct
epic/story rollup counts, accurate `rebar show <parent>` child lists, correct Jira hierarchy,
and archaeology for anyone later asking "what shipped under WS-B/WS-C/... ?". It buys nothing
for live scheduling.

That reframes the cost/benefit on `5992-f317-e05e-42f7` (the `parent` verb / `--force`): it
should be judged as a **general-purpose store-repair capability worth having on its own merits**,
not as an urgent unblock for this incident. And it argues strongly AGAINST the reopen ->
re-parent -> re-close workaround, which would risk 18 closed parents' status and ~95 reconcile
write events to fix a reporting-only defect.

This ticket should stay open (the edges are still missing and the ACs are unmet), but it can be
**de-prioritized** — nothing is blocked on it.

Operator decision (2026-08-06): closing without restoring the 59 parent edges.

Measured basis: all 59 orphaned children are ALREADY CLOSED, each with at least one commit in git log matching its full 16-hex ticket id. Nothing in the incident set is unfinished work. The lost edges cost hierarchical provenance only — e.g. story 60ce-29c1-58be-4648 should list 11 children and lists 2 — and cost nothing operationally: ready, next-batch and claim routing all operate on unclosed tickets, and both ends of every broken edge are closed. The layer above is intact (16 of 18 parents retain their own parent edge).

Restoration remains genuinely blocked: rebar edit --parent refuses a closed parent (_resolve_new_parent, src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:503-514), there is no force flag or parent verb, and 5992-f317-e05e-42f7 is still an idea. The only workaround — reopen, re-parent, re-close 18 closed parents — risks stranding them open and costs ~95 reconcile write events to repair a reporting-only defect.

The underlying CODE defect is fixed and closed separately (88d9-fe42-e50f-4067, landed 25ead49f3e), so no defect remains open. 5992 should now be judged on its own merits as a general store-repair capability, not as an urgent unblock for this incident.

Closed via --force-close because the acceptance criteria are written as 'restore all 59 edges' and are therefore literally unmet by design of this decision.

# 59 of the 63 tickets orphaned by the 2026-08-03 reconcile incident are STILL parentless

The **code defect** that destroyed these edges is fixed (`88d9-fe42-e50f-4067`, landed
`25ead49f3e`). The **data** was never restored. This ticket tracks that outstanding
restoration backlog, which no open ticket currently owns.

## What happened (re-confirmed independently in this investigation)

Reconcile run **30828160906** (GitHub Actions, `workflow_dispatch`, `MODE: live`,
2026-08-03 15:37:59-15:38:10 UTC) wrote 63 `EDIT` events with
`{"fields": {"parent_id": ""}}`, author `reconciler`, all in one commit
`b8062b10e97b0c891deefbefa87934bb37c66d84` on the `tickets` branch.

**All 63 destroyed a real parent edge. Zero were no-ops.**

The mechanism, cited:
* `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_field_diff.py:138-139` - outbound
  **OMITS** the parent field whenever the local parent's `ticket_type != "epic"`,
  so Jira is never told about it.
* `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py` `diff_inbound_parent` - inbound
  then read Jira's honest "no parent", classified it `PARENT_NO_PARENT`, and **CLEARED**
  the local edge. Its only guard, `should_propagate_removal`, answers the *outbound*
  question (absent locally -> delete on peer) and structurally cannot answer the inbound
  one. `add_managed_ref` is folded by the **local** parent-set event
  (`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:87-90`, `:526-528`), so "managed" never proved Jira
  ever had the parent.
* Omit-vs-clear asymmetry is documented on `39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b`.

**Discriminating evidence (this investigation).** Of tickets holding a parent immediately
before the run: **every one of the 63 lost parents is a `story` (62) or `bug` (1) - not one
`epic`**; 600+ epic-parented children in the same pass were untouched. Story/bug-parented
tickets that survived had **no Jira binding**, so the inbound differ never saw them. The rule
is exact: `cleared <=> bound AND parent is not an epic`. No unexplained residual.

## Why it was never repaired

`8b86-cf7f-ae1c-4955` - 61 of the 63 prior parents are **closed**, and
`rebar edit <child> --parent=<closed parent>` is refused by the `--parent` validation
cascade. `5992-f317-e05e-42f7` (a dedicated `parent` verb with `--force`) is still an
**`idea`**, so no repair route exists today.

## Current state (measured 2026-08-04)

* **59 of 63 still parentless**; 4 restored ad hoc.
* The full child -> lost-parent map is recoverable from the event log and is posted as a
  comment on this ticket.
* The `Reconcile Bridge` workflow is currently `disabled_manually` (last run
  2026-08-04 16:05 UTC), so nothing is re-clearing anything right now.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the recovered child -> lost-parent map is verified against the event log
- [ ] a supported write path exists for re-parenting onto a **closed** parent (depends on
      `5992-f317-e05e-42f7` / `8b86-cf7f-ae1c-4955`)
- [ ] all 59 remaining edges are restored, or each exception is recorded with a reason
- [ ] a post-restore sweep confirms 0 tickets from the incident set remain parentless
- [ ] restoration is done with the reconciler's peer-evidence fix in force, and a
      subsequent reconcile pass is confirmed not to re-clear them
